how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview platform/infrastructure team to identify where canonical configuration templates are stored and maintained
how_to_obtain.navigation: Ask: Where are the approved IaC templates stored? Are there separate repos for application and infrastructure configs? Who owns the template repository?
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Team can identify a specific repository URL with active maintenance and clearly defined ownership

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect CI/CD pipeline definitions to identify source repository references for infrastructure templates
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE '(git@|https://.*\.git|source.*=.*github|registry\.terraform\.io|helm repo add)' .github/workflows/ .gitlab-ci.yml Jenkinsfile 2>/dev/null | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Pipeline files reference a specific external or internal repository URL for template sourcing, confirming a template repository exists

option_description: Controls whether the configuration template repository uses a version control system (Git or equivalent) with full commit history, branches, tags, and change tracking to support template auditability and rollback capability.
security_impact: The Rego policy `operational_maintainability_of_config_templates` requires `input.version_control_enabled == true` alongside template repository existence. Without version control, template changes cannot be audited, rolled back, or reviewed — attackers or unauthorized users could modify configuration templates without detection, and configuration drift cannot be traced to its origin.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify the template repository has git initialized with commit history
how_to_obtain.command: git -C /path/to/template-repo log --oneline | wc -l && git -C /path/to/template-repo log --format='%H %ae %ad %s' --date=short | head -5
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-zero commit count with author, date, and message entries confirms version control is active with history

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for branch protection rules on the template repository via GitHub API
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GITHUB_TOKEN' 'https://api.github.com/repos/$ORG/$REPO/branches/main/protection' | jq '{required_reviews: .required_pull_request_reviews.required_approving_review_count, enforce_admins: .enforce_admins.enabled, status_checks: .required_status_checks.contexts}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON showing branch protection configuration with review requirements, confirming active version control governance

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the template repository commit history and tagging in GitHub/GitLab web interface
how_to_obtain.navigation: GitHub/GitLab > Template Repository > Commits tab > verify commits span multiple contributors and dates > Releases/Tags tab > verify tagged versions exist marking configuration baseline releases
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Repository shows a history of commits with meaningful messages, multiple contributors, and tagged releases corresponding to template versions

how_to_obtain.instruction: Verify git tags exist to mark versioned template releases
how_to_obtain.command: git -C /path/to/template-repo tag -l --sort=-version:refname | head -10 && git -C /path/to/template-repo log --tags --simplify-by-decoration --pretty='format:%d %s' | head -10
how_to_obtain.expected_output: List of semantic version tags (e.g., v1.2.0, v2.0.0) confirming versioned releases of configuration templates

typical_values: false (files stored in shared drive or wiki)
false (git repo exists but no enforced workflow or history)

option_description: Controls the breadth of infrastructure and environment types covered by centralized configuration templates, determining whether compute, network, storage, and application components all have approved templates or only a subset does.
security_impact: The Rego policy `operational_maintainability_of_config_templates` activates for both 'full' and 'partial' scopes when combined with other conditions, but 'partial' coverage leaves uncovered infrastructure components vulnerable to inconsistent or insecure ad-hoc configuration. 'none' fails the policy entirely, indicating no standardized provisioning exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate template directories in the template repository to identify covered infrastructure categories
how_to_obtain.command: find /path/to/template-repo -maxdepth 2 -type d | sort && ls -la /path/to/template-repo/modules/ 2>/dev/null || ls -la /path/to/template-repo/roles/ 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Directory listing showing categories like compute/, network/, storage/, database/, security-groups/, iam/ — absence of major categories indicates 'partial'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Count Terraform modules or Ansible roles by category to assess coverage breadth
how_to_obtain.command: find /path/to/template-repo -name 'main.tf' -o -name 'tasks/main.yml' | xargs -I{} dirname {} | sed 's|.*/||' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
how_to_obtain.expected_output: List of module/role names with counts; cross-reference against known infrastructure components to determine full vs. partial coverage

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview infrastructure team to map all deployed infrastructure component types against available templates
how_to_obtain.navigation: Create a coverage matrix: list all infrastructure types in production (VMs, containers, load balancers, databases, firewalls, IAM) and mark which have approved templates in the repository
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Coverage matrix showing >90% of component types templated = 'full'; <90% = 'partial'; 0% = 'none'

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the template repository README or documentation to find the stated coverage scope
how_to_obtain.navigation: Template Repository > README.md or docs/ folder > look for a coverage matrix, supported components list, or roadmap indicating which infrastructure types are currently templated
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation listing supported infrastructure components; if list covers all production infrastructure types, scope is 'full'

typical_values: partial (application layer only, no network/storage templates)

option_description: Controls whether configuration templates from the centralized repository are actively consumed by automated CI/CD or deployment pipelines, rather than being available but manually applied or ignored by engineers provisioning infrastructure.
security_impact: The Rego policy `operational_maintainability_of_config_templates` requires `input.deployment_pipeline_integrated == true` as a mandatory condition in both activation paths. Templates that exist but are not pipeline-integrated provide no enforcement guarantee — developers can bypass approved templates and provision infrastructure manually, reintroducing configuration drift and security baseline violations.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect CI/CD pipeline definitions for explicit references to the centralized template repository
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE '(template[-_]repo|infra[-_]repo|module.*source|chart.*repo|roles[-_]path|TF_VAR.*template)' .github/workflows/ .gitlab-ci.yml Jenkinsfile scripts/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^Binary'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Pipeline YAML lines showing module source references, Helm chart repository URLs, or Ansible roles path pointing to the centralized template repository

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check Terraform configuration for module source references pointing to the central template repository
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE 'source\s*=\s*"(git::|https://|registry\.terraform\.io|github\.com)' **/*.tf 2>/dev/null | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Module source declarations referencing the central template repository or Terraform registry confirm pipeline integration

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query CI/CD platform API to retrieve recent pipeline run configurations and verify template repository is referenced as a source
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GITLAB_TOKEN' 'https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/$PROJECT_ID/pipelines?per_page=5&status=success' | jq '.[].id' | xargs -I{} curl -s -H 'Authorization: Bearer $GITLAB_TOKEN' 'https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/$PROJECT_ID/pipelines/{}/jobs' | jq '.[].name' | sort -u
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Job names in recent successful pipelines that correspond to template application steps (e.g., terraform-apply, helm-deploy, ansible-playbook)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the deployment pipeline run history to confirm infrastructure provisioning jobs consume templates from the centralized repository
how_to_obtain.navigation: CI/CD platform (GitHub Actions/GitLab CI/Jenkins) > Project > Pipelines > Latest successful run > expand infrastructure provisioning job > review job logs for 'Downloading module', 'helm repo update', or 'roles_path' references to the template repository
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Pipeline job logs showing template or module fetching from the centralized repository URL before applying infrastructure changes

typical_values: true (pipelines fetch from central template repo)
